title: Reproduction
summary: How organisms reproduce sexually and asexually: human reproductive systems and the menstrual cycle, fertilization and IVF, and sexual reproduction in flowering plants.

keyterms.definition: Production of offspring from one parent by mitosis; offspring are genetically identical to the parent and each other.
Production of offspring by fusion of haploid gametes from two parents, generating genetically varied offspring.
Follicle-stimulating hormone from the anterior pituitary; stimulates follicle development and oestradiol secretion by the follicle wall.
Luteinizing hormone from the anterior pituitary; a surge triggers ovulation and development of the corpus luteum.
Ovarian steroid hormone that stimulates thickening of the endometrium; high levels stimulate the LH surge by positive feedback.
Hormone secreted by the corpus luteum (later the placenta) that maintains the endometrium and inhibits FSH and LH secretion.
Fusion of a male and a female gamete to produce a diploid zygote.
Fertilization of eggs by sperm outside the body, after hormone treatment to induce superovulation, followed by transfer of embryos to the uterus.
Transfer of pollen from an anther to a stigma.
Transfer of pollen from the anther of one plant to the stigma of a different plant of the same species.
Genetic mechanism preventing a plant's own pollen from fertilizing its ovules, avoiding inbreeding and maintaining genetic variation.
Start of growth of a seed's embryo into a seedling; requires water, oxygen and a suitable temperature.
Gonadotropin-releasing hormone from the hypothalamus; stimulates the anterior pituitary to secrete FSH and LH, initiating puberty.
Exocytosis of cortical granules from the egg after a sperm enters, hardening the zona pellucida to prevent polyspermy.
Hollow ball of cells formed from the zygote by repeated mitosis; implants in the endometrium about 7 days after fertilization.
Human chorionic gonadotropin, secreted by the early embryo; maintains the corpus luteum and is detected by pregnancy tests.

lessons.title: Sexual reproduction and the menstrual cycle

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes asexual from sexual reproduction?
options: Asexual reproduction involves meiosis; sexual reproduction involves only mitosis
Asexual reproduction produces genetically identical offspring; sexual reproduction produces genetically varied offspring
Asexual reproduction requires gametes from one parent; sexual reproduction requires gametes from two
Asexual reproduction only occurs in prokaryotes
questions.explanation: Asexual reproduction uses mitosis, so offspring are clones of one parent. Sexual reproduction combines gametes from two parents, producing variation. Many eukaryotes (e.g. strawberry runners, aphids) reproduce asexually.

questions.statement: Meiosis and fertilization both generate genetic variation in a sexual life cycle.
questions.explanation: Meiosis produces genetically different haploid gametes (crossing over and independent assortment), and random fusion of gametes from two parents creates new allele combinations. Meiosis also halves the chromosome number so fertilization restores diploidy.

questions.prompt: Which describes the difference between male and female gametes?
options: Female gametes are small, numerous and motile
Male gametes are large and contain food reserves
Male gametes are small, numerous and motile; female gametes are larger, fewer and contain food reserves
Both sexes produce gametes of similar size but in different numbers
questions.explanation: By definition the male sex produces many small, motile gametes (sperm) and the female sex produces fewer, large, non-motile gametes (eggs) with cytoplasm and food reserves for the early embryo.

questions.prompt: Match each structure of the human reproductive systems to its function.

pairs.right: Produces eggs and secretes oestradiol and progesterone
Site of fertilization; carries egg to uterus
Uterus lining where an embryo implants
Carries sperm from epididymis to urethra

questions.explanation: Gonads (testes and ovaries) produce gametes and sex hormones. Fertilization normally occurs in the oviduct, and the embryo implants in the endometrium.

questions.text: In the menstrual cycle, ___ from the anterior pituitary stimulates development of follicles in the ovary.
questions.explanation: FSH (follicle-stimulating hormone) stimulates follicle growth and the follicle wall's secretion of oestradiol. LH acts later to trigger ovulation.

questions.prompt: Put these events of the menstrual cycle in order, starting at the beginning of the cycle.
items: FSH rises and stimulates a follicle to develop
The developing follicle secretes increasing oestradiol
High oestradiol causes a surge in LH
Corpus luteum degenerates, progesterone falls and menstruation begins
questions.explanation: FSH starts follicle growth; the follicle's oestradiol rises until it triggers the LH surge (positive feedback), causing ovulation. The corpus luteum then secretes progesterone; if no pregnancy, it degenerates and the endometrium breaks down.

questions.statement: Progesterone from the corpus luteum inhibits FSH and LH secretion by negative feedback.
questions.explanation: High progesterone (with oestradiol) after ovulation inhibits pituitary FSH and LH secretion, preventing new follicle development while the endometrium is maintained.

questions.prompt: What is the effect of high oestradiol concentration just before ovulation?
options: It stimulates a surge of LH and FSH by positive feedback
It inhibits LH secretion by negative feedback
It causes the corpus luteum to degenerate
It causes the endometrium to break down
questions.explanation: Rising oestradiol from the maturing follicle switches from inhibiting to stimulating the pituitary, causing the mid-cycle LH (and FSH) surge — one of the few examples of positive feedback in the body.

questions.text: After ovulation, the remains of the follicle develop into the ___, which secretes progesterone.
questions.explanation: LH stimulates the empty follicle to become the corpus luteum, the source of progesterone that maintains the thickened endometrium.

questions.prompt: Why does menstruation occur at the end of a cycle without pregnancy?
options: FSH concentration rises sharply
LH stimulates the endometrium to shed
Oestradiol stimulates breakdown of the uterine lining
The corpus luteum degenerates, so progesterone falls and the endometrium is no longer maintained
questions.explanation: Progesterone maintains the endometrium. When the corpus luteum degenerates, progesterone drops, the lining breaks down, and the fall also removes inhibition of FSH so a new cycle starts.

questions.prompt: Which sequence describes fertilization in humans?
options: Sperm and egg nuclei fuse into one nucleus, which then divides by meiosis
Sperm and egg membranes fuse, the sperm nucleus enters, both nuclear membranes break down and the chromosomes join in one mitotic division
The whole sperm cell, including its tail, fuses with the egg nucleus
The sperm nucleus replaces the egg nucleus
questions.explanation: In humans the sperm and egg nuclei do not fuse into a single nucleus. Their nuclear membranes break down and all the condensed chromosomes take part in a joint mitosis, producing two diploid nuclei.

questions.statement: In IVF, the woman's normal secretion of FSH and LH is first suppressed by drugs.
questions.explanation: Down-regulation stops the natural cycle so the timing of egg production can be controlled. High doses of FSH are then injected to induce superovulation.

questions.prompt: Put the stages of IVF treatment in order.
items: Drugs suppress the woman's natural FSH and LH secretion
Eggs are collected from the follicles
Eggs are mixed with sperm in a dish
Embryos are transferred to the uterus
questions.explanation: IVF suppresses the natural cycle, stimulates many follicles with FSH, completes egg maturation with an hCG injection, then collects the eggs, fertilizes them in vitro and transfers embryos to the uterus.

questions.text: Using high doses of FSH to make many follicles develop at once is called ___.
questions.explanation: Superovulation gives many eggs from one cycle, increasing the chance of obtaining viable embryos.

questions.prompt: Match each part of an insect-pollinated flower to its role.

pairs.right: Contains ovules; develops into the fruit
Secretes sugary nectar to reward insects

questions.explanation: The anther (on a filament) forms the stamen; stigma, style and ovary form the carpel. Petals and nectaries attract and reward pollinating insects.

options: Fusion of a male gamete with an egg cell in the ovule
Growth of a pollen tube down the style
Transfer of pollen from an anther to a stigma
Dispersal of seeds away from the parent plant
questions.explanation: Pollination is only the transfer of pollen to a stigma. Fertilization happens later, after a pollen tube delivers the male gamete to the ovule; seed dispersal follows fertilization.

questions.statement: Having anthers and stigmas that mature at different times promotes cross-pollination.
questions.explanation: If pollen is released when the same flower's stigma is not receptive, self-pollination is reduced. Separate male and female flowers or plants have a similar effect.

questions.prompt: Why is self-incompatibility an advantage to a plant species?
options: It prevents inbreeding, so genetic diversity and vigour are maintained
It allows a plant to fertilize its own ovules more quickly
It increases the number of seeds produced by self-pollination
It ensures all offspring are genetically identical
questions.explanation: Self-pollination leads to inbreeding, which reduces genetic variation and increases homozygosity for harmful recessive alleles. Self-incompatibility stops pollen with a matching S-allele from fertilizing the ovule.

questions.text: After fertilization, the ovule develops into a ___.
questions.explanation: The ovule (containing the embryo) becomes the seed; the ovary around it becomes the fruit.

questions.prompt: Which set of conditions is generally required for seed germination?
options: Light, carbon dioxide and soil
Water, oxygen and a suitable temperature
Light, water and fertilizer
Carbon dioxide, oxygen and darkness
questions.explanation: Water rehydrates the seed and activates enzymes, oxygen allows aerobic respiration to release energy, and temperature must suit enzyme activity. Most seeds do not need light because they use stored food.

questions.prompt: What initiates the changes of puberty?
options: The ovaries and testes start secreting FSH
The anterior pituitary secretes GnRH, which acts on the gonads
Increased GnRH from the hypothalamus stimulates FSH and LH secretion, which stimulates sex steroid production
Testosterone from the hypothalamus stimulates the pituitary
questions.explanation: At puberty the hypothalamus increases GnRH secretion. GnRH stimulates the anterior pituitary to release FSH and LH, which stimulate the gonads to produce gametes and the steroid hormones testosterone or oestradiol.

questions.prompt: Put the stages of spermatogenesis in order.
questions.explanation: Both spermatogenesis and oogenesis involve mitosis, cell growth, two divisions of meiosis and differentiation.

questions.statement: In oogenesis, each meiosis produces four functional eggs.
questions.explanation: Cytoplasm divides unequally in oogenesis, so each meiosis gives one large egg and small polar bodies that degenerate. Spermatogenesis produces four sperm per meiosis.

questions.text: Enzymes released from the sperm's ___ digest a path through the zona pellucida.
questions.explanation: The acrosome reaction releases hydrolytic enzymes from the acrosome at the tip of the sperm head, allowing it to reach and fuse with the egg membrane.

questions.prompt: How is polyspermy prevented after one sperm has fused with the egg?
options: The acrosome of the first sperm releases enzymes that destroy other sperm
Cortical granules release their contents by exocytosis, hardening the zona pellucida
The egg undergoes mitosis immediately, expelling other sperm
Progesterone stops further sperm entering
questions.explanation: The cortical reaction makes the zona pellucida impenetrable, so only one sperm nucleus enters. Polyspermy would give an abnormal chromosome number.

questions.prompt: What does a pregnancy test detect?
options: Progesterone secreted by the corpus luteum
LH secreted by the pituitary
Oestradiol secreted by the placenta
hCG secreted by the embryo, detected with monoclonal antibodies
questions.explanation: Soon after implantation, the embryo secretes hCG, which appears in urine. Test strips carry monoclonal antibodies that bind hCG specifically.

questions.statement: hCG keeps the corpus luteum secreting progesterone in early pregnancy.
questions.explanation: hCG prevents degeneration of the corpus luteum, so progesterone stays high and the endometrium is not shed. Later the placenta takes over progesterone secretion.

questions.prompt: Match each stage of early pregnancy to its description.

pairs.right: Hollow ball of cells formed by mitosis
Exchanges materials between maternal and foetal blood

questions.explanation: The zygote divides to form a blastocyst, which implants about a week after fertilization. The placenta then supports foetal development until birth.

questions.text: During childbirth, uterine contractions stimulate more ___ secretion, an example of positive feedback.
questions.explanation: Stretching of the cervix triggers oxytocin release from the posterior pituitary; oxytocin causes stronger contractions, which cause more oxytocin release, until the baby is born. Falling progesterone removes inhibition of contractions.

questions.prompt: Early observational studies suggested HRT reduced coronary heart disease, but randomized trials found a slight increase. What best explains this?
options: Women taking HRT tended to have higher socio-economic status, a confounding factor that lowered heart disease risk
The randomized trials used too few participants
HRT changes its effect depending on the year of the study
Observational studies always overestimate risks
questions.explanation: A correlation does not show causation. HRT users differed from non-users in other ways (e.g. wealth, diet, exercise); randomized controlled trials remove such confounding and revealed the real effect.
